causal_chains.Scenario: Crude Charge Pump P-102A Bearing Failure Cascade
Preconditions: Continuous high crude processing rate (>102% nameplate capacity)
Lubrication particle contamination due to aging reservoir breather
Preventative maintenance overhaul deferred due to production quota targets
Weak Signals: Slight high-frequency vibration demodulation increase (0.45 to 1.2 gE)
Subtle bearing metal temperature rise (+6 C above seasonal baseline)
ISO cleanliness code degrading from 15/13/10 to 19/17/14
Abnormal Conditions: Overall vibration velocity RMS crosses 4.5 mm/s warning threshold
Audible cavitation and slight mechanical rubbing at suction eye
Escalation: Unmitigated run under high vibration causes bearing cage fracture
Axial shaft play destroys mechanical seal faces
causal_chains.Potential Outcome: Crude hydrocarbon leak, fire hazard, emergency unit shutdown
Preventive Opportunities: Immediate lubrication reservoir filtration upon particle count alert
Controlled load derate and transfer to standby pump P-102B within 7-day window
Enforced maintenance overhaul execution without commercial deferral

causal_chains.Scenario: Wet Gas Compressor Seal Degradation Under Utility Perturbation
Preconditions: Summer ambient heatwave elevating cooling water supply temperature to 34 C
High gas throughput demand from FCC and CDU fractionator
Weak Signals: Primary seal gas vent flow creeping upward (+0.1 Nm3/h per week)
Buffer nitrogen differential pressure regulator hunting
Abnormal Conditions: Primary vent flow exceeds alarm threshold (2.5 Nm3/h)
Secondary seal face temperature reaches 74 C
Escalation: Failure to boost buffer nitrogen pressure causes hydrocarbon migration into secondary vent
LEL gas detector GD-601 initiates unit shutdown alert
causal_chains.Potential Outcome: Toxic and flammable gas release to compressor shelter, emergency flare blowdown
Preventive Opportunities: Automated auxiliary cooling booster pump start
Proactive seal gas filter cartridge replacement and regulator tuning

causal_chains.Scenario: Crude Column Overpressure via Cooling Water Loss & Operator Overload
Preconditions: Cooling water pump electrical feed voltage sag trips running pump
Control room operator handling simultaneous alarm flood from 2 units
Weak Signals: Cooling water header pressure dips by 0.6 bar
Column overhead vapor temperature creeps upward (+4 C in 3 mins)
Abnormal Conditions: Column overhead pressure rises from 1.8 to 2.9 barg
Reflux accumulator drum liquid level approaches low-level trip
Escalation: Delayed manual startup of diesel standby CW pump due to task saturation
Pressure relief valves PSV-101A/B lift to flare header
causal_chains.Potential Outcome: Major flare emission event, off-spec product, column tray mechanical damage
Preventive Opportunities: Automated fast-bus transfer and auto-start for standby utility pumps
Dynamic alarm suppression during electrical transient events
